target.repo: tamarind-lend (local copy, not a git repository)

findings.cross_reference: IT Act 2000 s.43A and SPDI Rules 2011 (reasonable security practices; in force until 13 May 2027). RBI Cybersecurity Directions 2026.
findings.issue: The Android build embeds Verilane's live API key as a BuildConfig field, so it ships in every APK and comes out with a decompiler. Per docs/vendors/verilane-api.md:6-9, a live key can call every endpoint for the account, including GET /verifications/{reference}, which returns the extracted name, date of birth, address and document number with links to the stored images, and references are sequential. Anyone holding the APK can walk through every borrower's KYC record. Readiness gap under DPDP: s.8(5) and Rule 6 apply from 13 May 2027; the exposure is live today under IT Act s.43A.
findings.recommendation: Rotate the live key now in the Verilane dashboard (the old key stops at once). Remove VERILANE_API_KEY and VERILANE_BASE from build.gradle, route /ocr and /liveness through the Tamarind backend, and ask Verilane for endpoint-scoped or short-lived credentials. Get Verilane's access logs for /verifications and treat unexplained reads as a personal data breach (/dpdp-breach).

findings.cross_reference: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions 2025: need-based data collection with prior explicit consent (para 12 in the May 2025 text); RBI's digital lending rules also bar lending apps from reading contact lists and call logs. Applies: Tamarind is an NBFC lending through its own app. Verify paragraph numbers against RBI's current Master Direction.
findings.issue: To fill a two-reference picker, prepareSuggestions reads the whole address book and the last 90 days of the call log, and uploads every contact's name, number and call count before the borrower picks anyone (ReferencesStep.kt:17-24, api/onboarding.py:18-33). Non-reference rows stay in contact_graph and nothing deletes them. The notice lists only 'the two references you choose' (web/privacy-policy.html:20). Those contacts are Data Principals who got no notice and gave no consent, and no s.7 use covers them; across about 350,000 applicants the graph may also hold children's numbers (s.9). Readiness gap: these obligations apply from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Stop uploading the address book and call log. Use the Android contact picker so only the two chosen references leave the phone, drop READ_CALL_LOG and READ_CONTACTS from the manifest, and delete every non-reference row already in contact_graph. Say in the notice how references are used.

findings.cross_reference: RBI fair practices and recovery-conduct rules for NBFCs and the Digital Lending Directions 2025 (might apply to contacting third parties about a borrower's dues; verify the current paragraphs).
findings.issue: From 15 days past due, every morning, the job sends the reference_nudge SMS to up to five numbers from contact_graph for each overdue loan, ordered by reference flag and then call count. Once the two references are used, the rest go to contacts the borrower never chose. The message names the borrower and asks the recipient to get them to call about their account (config/sms-templates.yaml:2), which tells third parties the borrower has a problem account; to non-references it also says the borrower gave their number, which is untrue. The query has no upper limit on days past due, so the messages keep going daily after the account moves to Recoverline. Neither the borrower nor the contacts were told of this purpose. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Stop the job. If references are contacted at all, limit it to the two chosen references, tell the borrower at onboarding, confirm contact details only without naming the account, and cap the frequency. Remove the reference_nudge template.

findings.cross_reference: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions 2025: one-time access to location for onboarding or KYC, with explicit consent, and need-based collection (para 12 in the May 2025 text). Applies. Verify paragraph numbers.
findings.issue: The permission step asks for background location with the rationale 'Keep your account secure' and, if granted, schedules LocationSyncWorker to post the phone's position to about 1 metre every 6 hours with no end (PermissionsStep.kt:18, 26-28; LocationSyncWorker.kt:28-33; api/onboarding.py:48-58). Nothing cancels the worker when a loan closes or the borrower asks for erasure. The notice says location is taken once, during KYC, to confirm the city (web/privacy-policy.html:21), and the KYC rationale asks for fine location to confirm a city. The actual use is the in-house field visit plan, which routes agents to each overdue borrower's latest position (services/field_visits.py:7-24). Consent given for a different stated purpose is not informed or specific under s.6(1). Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Remove ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION and LocationSyncWorker, cancel the periodic work on installed apps, and take one coarse location at KYC as the notice says. Delete stored device_locations rows. Plan field visits from the address the borrower gave; if location is wanted for collections, ask for it separately with that purpose stated.

findings.cross_reference: Aadhaar Act 2016; RBI KYC Master Direction 2016 and PML Rules 2005: where Aadhaar authentication is not required, the customer redacts or blacks out the Aadhaar number. Applies; verify the current paragraph.
findings.issue: Aadhaar is accepted as an uploaded document, and the app asks for clear photos of the front and back with all four corners visible (KycUploadStep.kt:11), with no step to mask the number. accept_ovd stores both images as captured; only doc_number_masked in the database is masked. The full Aadhaar number therefore sits in the tamarind-kyc-docs bucket, which the credit_analyst and collections_partner console roles can read (config/rbac.yaml:9, 17). KMS encryption at rest does not limit who reads it through the console. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Mask the first eight digits before storage, either by asking the borrower to cover them or server-side from the OCR coordinates, and re-process existing Aadhaar images. Prefer DigiLocker, which kyc_records.method already allows.

findings.cross_reference: IT Act 2000 s.43A and SPDI Rules 2011 (financial information is sensitive personal data; in force until 13 May 2027).
findings.issue: When a statement fails to parse, handle_fi_ready logs the whole decrypted account aggregator payload (account profile, summary and six months of transactions) at WARNING. It lands in the api-app stream, kept 400 days and readable by the whole engineering group (deploy/logging.yaml:9-10, 19-21), a far wider audience than the credit_analyst role that bank_statements:read is granted to. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Log the consent ID, the error and a payload hash only. Purge api-app entries that hold FI payloads, and add a log filter that drops account and transaction structures.

findings.cross_reference: Account aggregator consent artefact: purpose 'Assess your loan application', one-time fetch (services/aa_client.py:13-21).
findings.issue: Every month offer_scoring reads all stored bank statements and loan history for every active and closed borrower and writes a pre-approved top-up limit, without checking offers_opt_in; only the push in jobs/offer_push.py checks it. The statements were fetched under an AA consent to assess one application, and the notice says only that opted-in borrowers' repayment history is used for offers (web/privacy-policy.html:25). Profiling borrowers who did not opt in, including former borrowers, from their bank data falls outside both. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Score only borrowers with offers_opt_in set, and only from repayment history, as the notice says. If bank data is wanted for top-ups, request a fresh AA consent for that purpose. Delete preapproved_offers rows for borrowers who have not opted in.

findings.cross_reference: Account aggregator consent artefact data life of 1 month (services/aa_client.py:20).
findings.issue: The retention schedule deletes bank statements when the data life in the borrower's AA consent ends, through jobs/retention.py (docs/retention-schedule.md:10). The consent template sets that data life to one month, but jobs/retention.py has no step for bank_statements or aa_consents, so full FI payloads are kept with no end. The code also has no handler for AA consent revocation or expiry: only the FI-ready notification is handled, and aa_consents.status never moves to revoked or expired. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Add a nightly purge of bank_statements past the consent's data life, keeping only the derived features the credit decision needs. Handle AA revoke and expiry notifications by stopping use and deleting the payload, and record the new status in aa_consents.

findings.issue: The schedule deletes rejected or withdrawn applications, with the applicant's KYC images, bank statements and references, 90 days after the decision (docs/retention-schedule.md:9). The job's DELETE joins applications to loans, and a rejected application never has a loan, so it deletes nothing. Withdrawn applications are not selected at all, and purge_kyc only reaches borrowers who had a loan. Rejected applicants' KYC images, selfies, bank statements and contact graphs are kept with no end. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Select applications with status rejected or withdrawn, decided more than 90 days ago and with no loan; for applicants with no other live application, delete kyc_records and the stored images, bank_statements, aa_consents, contact_graph and device_locations. Add a test with a rejected-applicant fixture.

findings.cross_reference: RBI outsourcing and recovery-agent rules for NBFCs and the Digital Lending Directions 2025 on sharing borrower data with recovery agents (might apply; verify).
findings.issue: The weekly hand-off selects b.* and writes every borrowers column into the CSV sent to Recoverline: email, date of birth, masked PAN, employer, monthly income, AA handle, the nominee's name and contact, the offers consent flag and more, plus names and numbers of up to five contacts from contact_graph (lines 12, 19-26). Schedule A of the agreement covers six fields: loan ID, name, mobile, address, outstanding amount and days past due (docs/vendors/recoverline-agreement.md:25-27). Data sent beyond the contract is not processed under a valid contract (s.8(2)), and the nominee and contacts have no ground for this disclosure at all. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Select the Schedule A columns by name, drop alt_contacts, and ask Recoverline to delete the extra fields from past files and certify it.

findings.issue: Clause 9 lets Recoverline keep Borrower Data for three years after the agreement ends and use it to improve its collection models across its clients. That use is Recoverline's own purpose, which makes it a Data Fiduciary for it with no ground from the borrowers, and the three-year tail conflicts with Tamarind's duty to have its processor erase data once the purpose is served (s.8(7)(b)). Nothing in the code or runbook tells Recoverline when an account is repaid, recalled or erased. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Amend clause 9: no use for Recoverline's own models, deletion within a short fixed period after each account's assignment ends, and deletion on Tamarind's instruction when a borrower's data is erased. Send recall and erasure notices from the hand-off job.

findings.issue: The collections_partner role, given to agency staff through vendor-provisioned named accounts, can read KYC documents, bank statements and the contact graph for every overdue account, not only accounts assigned to the agency at 60 days past due (config/rbac.yaml:1-2, 16-18). The agreement gives the agency six fields per assigned account, and the in-house collections role has none of these grants. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Cut collections_partner to the Schedule A fields on accounts currently assigned to Recoverline, and review the console-audit stream for partner reads of KYC documents and statements.

findings.cross_reference: RBI (Digital Lending) Directions 2025: data stored on servers in India, and data processed abroad brought back within 24 hours (para 13 in the May 2025 text). Applies. RBI Storage of Payment System Data circular 2018 might apply to repayment mandate data; verify.
findings.issue: A full copy of the tamarind-core database goes to ap-southeast-1 every day and is kept 35 days; the file describes it as the fallback if both India regions are lost (deploy/backup.yaml:15-21, docs/vendors/register.md:5). No country is restricted under s.16(1) yet, but s.16(2) keeps in force any Indian law that restricts transfers abroad, and RBI's digital lending rules require borrower data to stay on servers in India. Readiness gap: s.16 applies from 13 May 2027; the RBI requirement applies today.
findings.recommendation: Stop the cross-region copy or point it at an India region, delete the copies held in ap-southeast-1, and record backup locations in the data map. Get sign-off against the RBI Directions before adding any region outside India.

findings.issue: The breach runbook intimates every borrower affected (docs/runbooks/incident-response.md:18). Tamarind also holds personal data of people who are not borrowers: rejected applicants, the contacts and call counts in contact_graph, references and nominees. s.8(6) and Rule 7(1) require intimation to each affected Data Principal. The rest of the runbook covers the Board's initial intimation, the 72-hour report and the contents Rule 7(1) lists. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Change the row to every affected Data Principal, say how applicants, references, contacts and nominees are reached (the numbers held), and record what was tried when someone cannot be reached.

findings.issue: The notice says any consent can be withdrawn at Profile > Privacy as easily as it was given (web/privacy-policy.html:35). The only withdrawal endpoint is the offers switch (api/settings.py:13-26). Contacts, call log and location consents were each given with one tap (PermissionsStep.kt:21-25), but no route withdraws them or stops use of what was already uploaded: revoking the Android permission stops new reads, while the stored contact graph and location history stay in use for collections. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Add a withdrawal toggle for each permission-based consent under Profile > Privacy. On withdrawal, write a consent_events row, cancel LocationSyncWorker, and delete the borrower's contact_graph and device_locations rows.

findings.issue: DELETE /v1/me refuses everything while any loan is open, including the contact graph and location history that no law requires Tamarind to keep (services/rights.py:50-52). When it does run, it keeps the AA handle, nominee, employer, income, applications and repayment mandates without listing them in the retained explanation it returns, and it sends nothing to Recoverline, Verilane, Signalgrid or Pulsemetric, so processors keep their copies (s.8(7)(b)). Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: While a loan is open, still erase data held only on consent (contact graph, location, statements past their data life). Return the full list of what is kept and the legal reason for each item. Send erasure instructions to every processor that received the borrower's data and log the confirmations.

findings.issue: Two SDKs collect directly from the phone: Signalgrid (device model, OS, device identifiers, IP address, network type) and Pulsemetric (device identifiers, screen events, crash traces) (android/app/build.gradle:39-42, docs/vendors/register.md:9-10). The signup consents cover credit_assessment and offers only (config/app.yaml:11-18), and no consent event is recorded for either SDK. The notice gives device data the purposes of detecting fraud and fixing crashes (web/privacy-policy.html:22) and does not mention screen analytics. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: List screen analytics in the notice as its own purpose and start Pulsemetric analytics only after a separate opt-in recorded in consent_events. Record the consent relied on for Signalgrid's fraud checks.

findings.issue: The bulk SMS gateway receives borrower numbers, loan amounts and days past due, and borrower names in messages to contacts. It is not named in the vendor register, and its 2024 services agreement is the only listed contract without processing terms (docs/vendors/register.md:11). The payment aggregator whose card token reference is stored in repayment_mandates (db/migrations/0006_repayment_mandates.sql:5) is not in the register at all. Processing and security terms for both are not found in the reviewed material. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Name both vendors in the register, confirm whether each acts as Tamarind's processor, and put processing terms with security safeguards, breach notice and deletion clauses in place with the SMS gateway.

findings.issue: risk_admin holds every grant over all data (config/rbac.yaml:20-22). How many people hold the role is not in the reviewed material. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: List the holders, split the role into the grants each job needs, and review its use in the console-audit stream every quarter.

findings.issue: PATCH /v1/me lets a borrower correct email, address, employer and monthly income only. Name, date of birth and mobile number have no correction route, while the notice offers correction of all data (web/privacy-policy.html:36). Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Add a correction request for name, date of birth and mobile number that goes through re-verification (KYC or OTP) instead of a direct update.

findings.issue: The access export (GET /v1/me/data) covers the profile and nine tables but not preapproved_offers, the top-up limit Tamarind computes about the borrower every month. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Add preapproved_offers to EXPORT_TABLES and describe the monthly scoring in the summary returned.

findings.issue: The escalation note in the grievance configuration, which reads as the text sent to complainants, points only to the RBI Ombudsman after 30 days (config/support.yaml:5). The published notice does name the Data Protection Board (web/privacy-policy.html:41), and a complainant who has used the grievance route may go to the Board (s.13(3)). Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Add the Data Protection Board route for personal data complaints to the escalation note, as the notice already does.

findings.issue: The test fixture holds borrower records with identifier-shaped values: full names, emails, Indian-format mobile numbers, dates of birth, masked PAN and document numbers. The README calls everything synthetic and the values look like placeholders (reserved example.test domain, zero-filled numbers), but this was not verified. Readiness gap: applies from 13 May 2027.
findings.recommendation: Keep fixtures visibly synthetic: generate them from a seeded generator with reserved ranges, and add a check that fails on numbers in live mobile ranges.
